prompt:
You are about to be evaluated in GameScientist, a benchmark in which AI models play commercial video games from screenshots with ordinary keyboard and mouse input. Before the run starts we would like to interview you. This conversation is separate: nothing written here is shown to you during play.

Model under test: jev-1.14.0 (served at api.typesafe.ai).
Game: PEAK.
About the game: PEAK is a first-person climbing survival game. A fresh attempt begins at the title screen, continues through an airport and then an island expedition. Ascending through successive regions leads toward the summit. An expedition can end in native victory or loss. The island rotates daily.
Controls:
WASD moves; Shift sprints or leaps while climbing; Space jumps; Control crouches; E interacts; Q drops or throws (hold); 1-3 selects item slots, 4 selects the backpack, and Tab stashes the selected item. The mouse turns the view or operates menus; left mouse climbs or uses an item, right mouse offers a helping hand or alternate item use. Escape opens the menu. When fully downed, hold the interaction key E to give up. Shared aliases: arrow keys move the mouse at 600 pixels per second; J and K hold left and right mouse respectively. Native free mouse and keyboard actions remain available to the language model.
Choose one ordinary input from the current screenshot. Keys are held for one second and released. Arrow keys and J/K are deterministic mouse aliases available to both cohorts. In gameplay the mouse turns the view; in menus it moves the cursor. These descriptions explain controls only.
Group input:
  forward: Hold W to walk forward.
  back: Hold S to walk backward.
  left: Hold A to strafe left.
  right: Hold D to strafe right.
  forward_left: Hold W and A to move diagonally forward and left.
  forward_right: Hold W and D to move diagonally forward and right.
  sprint: Hold W and left Shift to run forward.
  jump_climb: Hold Space to jump or hold onto a climbable surface.
  forward_climb: Hold W and Space together to move forward and jump or climb.
  crouch: Hold left Control to crouch.
  interact: Hold E to interact; when fully downed, hold the same interaction key to give up.
  primary: Hold J, the shared left-mouse alias, to climb or use the held item.
  secondary: Hold K, the shared right-mouse alias, to offer a helping hand or use the alternate item action.
  look_left: Hold Left, a shared input alias that moves the mouse left at 600 pixels per second.
  look_right: Hold Right, a shared input alias that moves the mouse right at 600 pixels per second.
  look_up: Hold Up, a shared input alias that moves the mouse upward at 600 pixels per second.
  look_down: Hold Down, a shared input alias that moves the mouse downward at 600 pixels per second.
  drop: Hold Q to drop or throw the selected item.
  menu: Press Escape to open or close the menu.
  slot_1: Press 1 to select inventory slot 1.
  slot_2: Press 2 to select inventory slot 2.
  slot_3: Press 3 to select inventory slot 3.
  slot_4: Press 4 to select the backpack slot.
  click_target: Left-click the visible menu button or interface control you locate.
  point_target: Move the pointer onto a visible interface element without clicking.
  stash: Press Tab to stash the selected item in the backpack.
  forward_primary: Hold W and the left mouse button (J alias) to move forward while climbing or using the held item.
  climb_leap: Hold left Shift and the left mouse button (J alias) to leap while climbing.
How you will play: each turn you see one screenshot and choose one action; the game is paused while you think, then each action uses a nominal 1 s host-time step. Input is released before any integration-specific rendering wait, then the game pauses again. Native simulation time depends on speed, native pause and performance. Rendering waits consume the same wall-clock budget. The run lasts 2 hours of wall-clock time, including your thinking time. If the game ends your attempt, it restarts within the same time budget and you keep notes from earlier attempts.
Scoring: 100 points, awarded only from the game's own saved progress, each milestone at most once:
- Reach 10 native meters above the verified beach starting height while conscious in the same expedition (10 points)
- Reach 25 native meters above the verified beach starting height while conscious in the same expedition (10 points; requires rise-10m)
- Reach 50 native meters above the verified beach starting height while conscious in the same expedition (10 points; requires rise-25m)
- Reach 100 native meters above the verified beach starting height while conscious in the same expedition (10 points; requires rise-50m)
- Reach 200 native meters above the verified beach starting height while conscious in the same expedition (10 points; requires rise-100m)
- Complete SHORE and advance the native map segment to the second region while conscious (10 points)
- Complete the day's second region, including its native variant, and advance to ALPINE in the same expedition (10 points; requires shore-complete)
- Complete ALPINE and advance to CALDERA in the same expedition (10 points; requires second-region-complete)
- Complete CALDERA and advance to THE KILN or beyond in the same expedition (10 points; requires alpine-complete)
- The native local character statistics confirm expedition victory after the final ascent; a model claim or entering the summit scene is insufficient (10 points; requires caldera-complete)

Please answer four questions:
1. What score out of 100 do you expect to reach, and how likely (0-100%) is it that you reach at least that score?
2. How likely (0-100%) is it that you reach the full 100 points?
3. What do you expect to be the hardest part, and where are you most likely to fail?
4. Which game mechanics work in your favour, and which work against you?
Reply with one JSON object only:
{"expected_score": 0-100, "expected_score_probability": 0-100, "full_score_probability": 0-100, "hardest_part": "...", "likely_failure": "...", "helpful_mechanics": "...", "harmful_mechanics": "..."}
